description: Analyzes Yu Hua’s To Live through Fugui’s framed oral account, the changing meaning of his lost inheritance, preventable and contingent family deaths, and Jiazhen’s refusal to demand further suffering. Compares the novel’s ending with Zhang Yimou’s film and considers the role of translation, resisting both a simple moral fable and a consoling story of historical progress.
